nomoonlightthisnight.text: NoMoonlightThisNight fights like the night shift never ends: upper tier across almost the whole card, quick on the trigger, and still pushing hard when the opposition gets serious. Against the toughest third the edge thins a little, the one soft spot in an otherwise sharp card. The lifetime board and the matchups tell the same story, end of story.

ninjiom.text: NinJiom has been fighting since 2014 and still sits near the very top: matchup rating near the top, activity right there with it, and resistance sitting with the very best. The accuracy and headshot share both sit above the middle, and the lifetime board echoes the matchups. A veteran who still shows up sharp.

niiliill.text: NIIlIIll is a young account with the surest aim around: among the very best tracked, landing nearly every shot, yet the headshots stay rare. The output holds mid-pack against stronger opposition. The edge against the strongest third stays high. Early read, and the lifetime board already undersells the matchup game.

ncjimbob.text: NCJimBob has been at this since 2014, and the years show in the patience: unhurried on the trigger, yet the matchup kill-death line stands with the best of them. The resistance is elite — few absorb strong opposition this well — and the edge holds against the strongest third too. The lifetime IvI sits middling, and headshots are rare, but the matchups tell the truer story.

neoncreeper2.text: Neoncreeper2 picks the moment, then cashes in: the matchup kill-death line ranks among the elite, and the lifetime kill-death line agrees. The headshots are rare and the aim is ordinary, yet the results keep coming. The lifetime IvI reads below average — a split board, with the matchups telling the truer story.

nothoughts.text: NoThoughts arrived in 2015 and never left: top shelf across the board, a trigger that stays steady, and an appetite that swells as the heat rises. The aim holds, the headshots land, and the career tally backs up the matchups. A strong regular, end of story.

nouturns.text: NoUTurns wins the fights they pick and lets the rest go: bravery merely above average, yet a matchup kill-death mark sitting among the very best tracked, resistance right there beside it. The pace is middling, the aim sits mid-pack, and headshots are rare — yet the results stay elite. Meanwhile the lifetime board rests near the bottom, and the matchups paint a far brighter picture than the lifetime numbers.

nanikouliwa.text: Nanikouliwa has kept a top-shelf game since 2014: rating, activity, bravery, and resistance — all of it near the very top, with the matchup kill-death line holding its own. The game keeps climbing as the opposition improves; the edge stands up against the strongest third too. The aim sits mid-pack, but headshots run above average while the lifetime board matches.

neoncreeper1.text: Neoncreeper1 has been around since 2013, and the card shows a survivor: resistance and matchup kill-death both in the top ranks, with a lifetime kill-death mark to match. The game does not climb as the opposition improves, and the lifetime board rates them below the matchups. Still, the results hold up — a veteran who endures whatever the fight brings.

nickiovs.text: NickioVS is the quiet metronome of the upper tier: nearly every measure lands at the top, from matchup rating to pace to aim. Bravery climbs with the opposition, never wilting, and resistance holds firm against the strongest attacks. Consistency sits mid-pack, the one line that keeps the card from a clean sweep. A steady, complete fighter since 2022, with no soft spot anywhere else.

nuil.text: nuIl wins the aim duel before the fight starts: accuracy among the finest tracked, with a furious work rate and a game that keeps rising as the opposition hardens. The matchup numbers sit near the top on every line, and the resistance barely bends against stronger enemies. Headshots are rare here, so the body-shot precision does the talking, and the lifetime board undersells the matchups.

nucleartouch.text: Nucleartouch has been carving up battlefields since 2013: tempo, nerve, and staying power all in the top tier, with a head-to-head kill-death figure to match and accuracy to burn. Headshots are scarce, yet the kills keep coming at a furious rate. The lifetime board rates them far below the matchups — the long record undersells a player the recent fights rank among the best.

narcoticjason.text: NarcoticJason has been at this since 2013, and the card shows why they stuck around: bravery and resistance near the top, with a matchup kill-death mark and lifetime kill-death record to match. Activity is above average, the pace strong, and the aim above average too. Consistency sits mid-pack — the one line that doesn't climb with the rest.

ncloveszmester.text: NCloveszmester has been winning the hard way since 2013: near the top of the matchup board; a shell that holds against rapid finishers and a faceoff kill-death tally behind it. The pace sits mid-pack, the aim ordinary, the headshot share near the bottom — yet the matchups stay near the top. Consistency against the hardest third holds up well, which is the mark of results earned the slow way.

neildamnstrong.text: NeilDamnstrong has been a fixture since 2016, and the record reads like one: near the top of the matchup board, with staying power against quick-killing opposition and a head-to-head kill-death line to match. The pace sits well above average, the aim merely ordinary, and the lifetime board lands a notch below them. When the opposition gets toughest, the edge thins, the one wrinkle in a long, steady career.

neruvon.text: Neruvon brings a full toolkit to every fight: top-tier in the matchups, hot in tempo, and bravery that grows as the field gets tougher. On the duels, the engagement kill-death ratio sits well above average. The career ledger lands mid-pack, but tempo is the calling card here, turning ordinary exchanges into winning ones. A strong regular who rarely gives a fight away.

notoupee.text: NoToupee's game is sharp and patient: top-tier in the matchups, even in tempo, bravery holding firm as the opposition hardens. The bout kill-death tally rides near the top, and the aim runs above the pack. Against the meanest slice the edge thins out, the single soft spot on an otherwise strong card. The lifetime board sits mid-pack, a shade more restrained than the duels suggest.

nuclearreactorru.text: NuclearReactorRu is the matchup board's loud surprise: top-tier on the ratings, fierce in tempo, and a clash kill-death line near the top. The lifetime board tells a different tale, with the IvI line sitting near the bottom and headshots almost never landing. When the sternest third arrives, the edge thins out fast, the one crack in an otherwise fierce card. The duels are the steadier truth here.

nlrao.text: NlraO never waits for the fight to come to them: in the top bracket of the matchup board, with quick hands, and still charging when the stakes climb. The headshot share is high, and the lifetime board paints the same picture. Nothing showy, just a player turning up ready, fight after fight.

nuli.text: nulI plays a deliberate game: at the top of the matchup board, unhurried on the trigger, and unbothered when the heat rises. The accuracy does the talking here, precise and calm, with resistance that barely bends. A player with a plan, and the results to back it up.

n7jpicardo.text: N7jpicardo plays a balanced, bruising game: a matchup rating in the top bracket, resistance that keeps its shape, and a lifetime kill-death tally sitting near the top. The lifetime IvI sits mid-pack, a touch below the matchups. The edge keeps its shape when the opposition turns toughest. A steady regular who wins more exchanges than they lose.

n0tagaln.text: N0tAgaln turns up in the thick of it and rarely leaves empty-handed: a matchup rating in the top tier, resistance to match, and a kill pace that runs just as high. The lifetime ledger tells the same story, the edge holds steady as the opposition hardens, and only consistency stays ordinary. A dependable presence, sharp where it counts, and still climbing.

nanazhang.text: nanazhang plays a balanced, no-frills game: sitting above the middle of the matchup board, with bravery, resistance, and a direct-fight kill-death record all holding up against stronger opposition. The lifetime numbers sit in the middle as well. Aim and headshots land mid-pack too — steady, unspectacular, and always there.

nimanantaoyishavs.text: NIMANANTAOYISHAVS plays a fast, fearless game: above the pack on the matchup board, settled as enemies get stronger, and a tempo that never drops. The lifetime kill-death line runs near the top, ahead of the matchups — the flashy part of an otherwise solid card. A regular who runs toward the hardest fights and usually wins them.

nanayashiy.text: NanayaShiy brings a complete game with no single headline: well above average across the matchup board, steady as enemies toughen, and a matchup kill-death count that sits above the middle. The aim is sharp, the tempo holds, and headshots land at a middle-of-the-road rate. The lifetime board runs a touch more modest than the matchups, but the record reads as a strong, dependable regular.

necronxv2.text: NecronXV2 has been setting the pace since 2017: a tempo near the summit, bravery that keeps rising as enemies toughen, and a kill pace to match. The aim is sharp, headshots land near the top, while the lifetime IvI runs just under the summit. The matchup rating runs well above average, and consistency holds above the middle — a veteran card with barely a wrinkle.

nullfunction.text: nullfunction has been around since 2012, and the years show in a game with no soft edge: well above average across the matchup board, steady as the opposition strengthens, and a duel record that holds up just as well. The own pace runs above average, the aim lands well, and headshots find their mark more often than most. The lifetime IvI line sits near the top — a long career that still reads strong.

nannystate.text: NannyState threads the needle with unusual precision: accuracy near the top, a duel kill-death ledger to match, and a matchup rating well above average. The shots rarely land high, yet they land where they count. The lifetime board paints a dimmer picture than the matchups, which makes the matchup card the truer read — a sharp, steady regular whose edge dips a touch against the hardest third.

noobek1.text: Noobek1 is the card the lifetime board undersells: matchup rating, tempo, bravery, and resistance all well above average, with the even-fight kill-death tally to match. The aim sits mid-pack and headshots trail near the bottom, while consistency dips below average. The lifetime board lands below average too — proof that the matchups, not the lifetime totals, tell the truer story here.

nagibatbich.text: NAGIBATbICH plays a patient, picking game: the lifetime kill-death line sits among the very best tracked, with resistance near the top and a head-to-head kill-death tally to match. Bravery sits mid-pack — the fights come on their own terms, not every brawl. The lifetime IvI line stays middling, so the board flatters a little, and the edge falls near the bottom when the opposition gets toughest.

nowysz.text: nowysz has been at this since 2012, and the card reads like a long, steady career: rating, activity, bravery, resistance, and the matchup kill-death line all well above average. The lifetime board agrees, the pace holds up, and only consistency sits mid-pack. Headshots land mid-pack too, the one ordinary line on an otherwise strong record.

narmolo.text: Narmolo brings the fight to the strongest opposition and usually wins it: the direct-fight kill-death record near the top, resistance above average, and a lifetime kill-death line keeping pace. Consistency sits near the bottom against the toughest third, and headshots land below average. A veteran since 2016 with a card built on winning hard fights.

nicejokeer.text: NiceJOkeer owns a card full of contradictions: a lifetime kill-death line among the very best tracked, paired with a kill pace below average. Resistance sits near the top and the matchup kill-death tally with it, yet the lifetime rating lands below average. A veteran since 2018 who wins enormous fights at a walking pace.

ncdawulnc.text: NCDawulNC brings a game with no headline and no hole: matchups comfortably above the middle, brisk on the trigger, and holding up as foes get stronger. The lifetime ledger lands mid-pack, a touch below what the matchups promise. When the fight gets hardest, the edge gives a little ground — the single soft seam on a veteran's card since 2014.

nsgdxoc.text: NSGDXoc shoots straight and wins the duels: accuracy near the summit, a one-on-one kill-death line near the summit, and a matchup grade sitting clear of the middle. Headshots rarely land, which makes the accuracy the stranger half of the pair. Lifetime numbers sit mid-pack, below what the matchups promise. A veteran since 2015, still sharp.

nightbvs.text: NightBVs is a study in contrasts: accuracy near the top, yet headshots near the bottom, and a lifetime IvI that lands below average. The matchup rating lands comfortably clear of average, carried by a kill-death ledger near the top. Consistency sits near the bottom too — a card full of sharp edges and open questions.

netraamnc.text: netraamNC has been setting the pace since 2015, and the card still runs hot: well above average across the board, with a tempo near the very top that never lets up. The edge holds firm as the opposition gets stronger — the mark of a game that travels. A veteran who turns up ready, fights hard, and leaves the other side chasing.

nightmarechi1d.text: NIGHTMAREChi1d has fought since 2018 with the sharpest headshot game on the card: headshots land near the very top, and the lifetime IvI keeps pace beside them. The matchup rating sits well above average, with tempo, bravery, and resistance holding there too. A veteran whose shots find the mark more than nearly anyone's, and whose results have held up for years.

nullpointvalue.text: NullPointValue has played since 2017 at full tilt: tempo, kill pace, and aim all sit near the top, while the lifetime IvI keeps pace with them. Bravery and resistance hold well above average beside that speed, yet the toughest-third edge fades below average against the hardest opposition. A veteran who runs every fight at a sprint and pays for it only against the very best.

n1kkos.text: N1KkOS is a puzzle with a sharp edge: the duel record sits near the top, and the matchup rating and tempo both run well above the middle. The resistance weathers harder-hitting foes, yet against the strongest third the edge falls away almost entirely. The lifetime sheet sits near the bottom, the aim is rough, and headshots scarce — a card that dazzles in the matchups and fades everywhere else.

nastyrhinoplastynso.text: NastyRhinoplastyNSO brings the same solid game to every fight: the matchup rating, tempo, and nerve all land well above the middle. The resistance stands up to heavier fire. They come out ahead in direct fights more often than not, and the headshot share runs above the middle. The lifetime record agrees with the matchups, and there is no weak seam anywhere — just a dependable regular who keeps delivering.

nnnt.text: NNNT plays a bright, balanced game: the matchup rating clears the middle, the tempo runs well above it, and the nerve holds firm. They bank more kills than deaths in direct fights, the headshots land near the top, and the lifetime board sits right up there too. The lifetime exchange ratio alone lands mid-pack — the one ordinary line on a strong card.

notabotanana.text: NotaBotaNana plays a solid, unspectacular game: the matchup mark, tempo, and nerve all land above the middle. The resistance stays solid when enemies hit back harder. Their duel arithmetic runs favorable, the aim is average, and headshots land mid-pack. The lifetime board lands right in the middle too — a regular whose matchup game runs a step ahead of the career numbers.

notanyday.text: Notanyday is a steady hand in every fight: strong across the matchup board, calm against stronger opposition, and accurate enough to make it count. Headshots come at a middling rate, and the long-run board tells the same story. A reliable regular who turns up, holds their ground, and gets the job done.

newplayertr.text: newplayerTR plays a game built on staying power: a matchup grade a good cut above the middle, unmoved while the fight turns rough, and the edge holding firm against the hardest third. Their kill returns from head-to-head fights sit mid-pack, while the lifetime kill-death line runs well above average. The accuracy is ordinary, but the headshots land well above average. A regular whose patience outlasts the other side.

nutj0b.text: NUTJ0B wins the duels and loses the paperwork: the matchup kill-to-death count sits near the very top, with rating, activity, bravery, and resistance all well above average. The aim and the headshots both land below average, and the lifetime board lands below average too, a cooler read than the matchups. When the opposition gets hardest, the edge slips a little, the one wrinkle in a card that otherwise fights above its weight.

nariea.text: Nariea arrived this year and already plays like a fixture: a matchup rating well into the upper tier, quick to the next fight, and calm as the enemies improve. The lifetime numbers sit with the very best, with headshots doing much of the talking. Take this one as an early sketch, drawn from a smaller, older set of matchups.

nirmata.text: NIRMATA wins the hard way: an upper-tier matchup rating built on resistance near the very top, while the aim itself sits near the bottom. The lifetime board undersells them badly, landing below average where the matchups see strength. A patient, stubborn card that gets its results the unglamorous way.

nightdream.text: NightDream plays a fast, front-foot game: above average on the matchup card, brisk tempo, and results that land above average in genuine exchanges. The results thin out against the hardest opposition, the one crack in the card. The lifetime board tells a middler story, but the matchups are the livelier truth.

neji42300.text: Neji42300 has been at it since 2014, and the card shows a player who settled into a strong groove long ago: a strong overall rating, a steady tempo, and holds firm against stronger opposition. The lifetime numbers and the matchups agree, with accuracy and headshots both comfortably above the middle. A seasoned regular, still showing up and still holding their own.

nimadedan.text: NiMaDeDan plays a patient, precise game: a clear step above the pack overall, a measured tempo, and steady nerves as the opposition gets stronger. The direct-duel record tilts their way, and the accuracy sits comfortably above the middle. The headshots are the modest part, and the edge fades a little against the strongest opposition. The overall story stays a strong, composed regular.

nuclearpowered.text: NuclearPowered runs hot and keeps running: a sturdy overall rating, a top-shelf tempo, and thrives against stronger opposition. But the pace, the accuracy, and the lifetime IvI line all sit near the very top — a high-energy game that rarely lets up. The head-to-head record lands mid-pack, a step behind the rest of the card.

nighthade.text: Since 2014, Nighthade has played a steady, well-rounded game: above the average line in the matchups, unbothered when stronger opponents show up, and sharp enough to land the headshots that matter. The lifetime board paints a slightly more modest picture than the matchups. A veteran regular who keeps turning up and keeps the fight honest.

n1kk0r.text: N1Kk0R plays a sharp, uneven game: a step clear of the pack in the matchups, quick through each exchange, and willing to meet stronger opposition head-on. The head-to-head tally lands above average, yet the aim stays below it — accuracy below average, headshots near the bottom — so the kills come from aggression, not precision. The lifetime IvI line sits near the bottom too, while the kill-death board stays strong. A fiery regular whose results outrun the raw aim.

newstar003.text: Newstar003 wins fights with placement rather than headshots: a clear notch above the middle across the matchup board, brisk through each exchange, and calm when the duels turn hard. Accuracy lands near the top of the tracked population, yet headshots stay below average, so the kills come from clean, patient shooting. The career numbers paint a quieter picture than the duels, landing mid-pack where the recent fights look stronger.

nikkusu.text: Nikkusu plays a complete, up-tempo game: well above average across almost the whole card, brisk through exchanges, and calm when the opposition toughens. The aim is clean, the headshot share is not — few of the shots that land find the head, the one quiet gap in the card. The lifetime board tells the same story as the matchups. A long-serving regular since 2016, still sharp, still reliable.

nsenvirnment.text: NSEnvirnment is the steady hand in the room: well above average across the rating, the pace, and the lifetime board, while the matchup tally sits mid-pack. Unfazed as the opposition sharpens, measured enough to pick the right moment. A strong regular, the kind whose card never lies about them.

ncnp.text: NCNP is barely a month into the record and already plays like a regular with a plan: well above average on the overall rating, a brisk tempo, and steady as the opposition gets sterner. The results stay level no matter how stern the other side gets, and in head-to-head matchups the kill tally runs near the top. The headshots land more often than most, while the raw accuracy sits mid-pack, a sign the aim is still catching up to the instincts. Early read, but the opening pages carry weight.

ncx001.text: NCx001 shoots straight and wins steady: among the most accurate tracked, fast hands, and unruffled as the opposition hardens. Their direct duels sit squarely mid-pack, and the lifetime view runs a touch ahead of them. Headshots come rarely, which makes the accuracy all the more telling — precision over flash, every time.

nspleasuremodel.text: NSPleasureModel plays a measured game: sitting a notch above the middle where it counts, unhurried on the trigger, and composed when the fight thickens. The aim sits in the middle of the pack and headshots come less often than most. Nothing flashy — just a regular who reads the fight well and keeps the ledger tilted their way.

nanolithography.text: Nanolithography plays at a relentless pace: above average overall, undaunted as the opposition improves, and elite for tempo and headshots. The resistance is middling and the edge fades under the heaviest pressure, though the accuracy stays high and the lifetime board climbs near the summit. A high-energy regular who keeps the pressure on from the first exchange to the last.

nerovs.text: NeroVS plays at full throttle: upper tier in the matchups, fearless as the opposition improves, and among the very best at turning fights into kills. The accuracy is elite, the tempo relentless, and the lifetime IvI line sits near the summit. Against the fiercest opposition the results dip a touch, the only soft spot in a loud, confident game.

nira0.text: Nira0 has played a high-tempo game since 2016: above average in the matchups, unfazed when the opposition improves, and among the very best for pace and headshots. The duel ledger rests mid-pack and the edge thins in the toughest exchanges, but the lifetime board runs near the summit. A veteran who still sets a blistering pace and still makes every fight a chase.

nerathos.text: Since 2013, Nerathos has been a fixture of the middle-upper game: well above average overall, spry through the exchanges, and unshaken as the opposition strengthens. The pace sits above the middle, the matchup tally matches the career kill tally, and nothing on the game looks fragile. A veteran regular, still turning up and still holding the standard high.

nimeiya.text: Nimeiya arrived in 2025 and already plays like a fixture: calm under pressure, strong against rising opposition, and consistent enough that the hard fights look no different from the easy ones. The matchup exchange is still middle of the pack, with plenty of road ahead. Accuracy is the calling card so far.

ncxoliver.text: NCxOliver plays at full sprint: the tempo sits near the very top, the aim matches it, and the duels tilt their way more often than not. The shine fades against the fiercest opposition, where the results drop off sharply. Still, the lifetime IvI line stands near the top, which suits a fast, fearless regular who never waits for permission to push.

nosferatotr.text: nOsferatoTR brings steady heat to every fight: well above average on the matchup front, quick-handed, and dangerous when a headshot opens the exchange. The form wobbles against the strongest opposition, the one clear crack in the profile. The lifetime figures paint a slightly brighter picture than the matchup return, and the finish stays warm: a reliable regular with bite.

nakurwiatorka.text: Nakurwiatorka picks fights with care: well above average on the whole, with staying power above mid-pack; the matchup record matches. The pace is unhurried, and when the opposition turns fiercest, the form dips. Still, the lifetime figures line up with the matchups, and the headshots sit mid-pack. A thoughtful regular who wins by choosing well rather than charging in.

netraam.text: Netraam arrived back in 2014, and the game still comes naturally: well above average overall, with courage and staying power clear of mid-pack. The matchup tally stands above average too, and the tempo keeps up. Against the fiercest opposition the edge fades a touch, the one wrinkle in a long, steady career. A regular who has seen it all and still shows up sharp.

nierti.text: Nierti has fought since 2014 with the same patient recipe: well above average across the board, staying power well clear of mid-pack, with a matchup line that agrees. The pace stays even, and when the fiercest opposition arrives, the results sag a little. The lifetime marks sit close to the matchups, which leaves the picture clear. A seasoned regular who wins by picking the right moments.
